acceptanceCriteria: the owner chooses (a), (b) or (c) and the decision is recorded

for (a)/(b): both tests pass 20 consecutive runs at load ~60 with no assertion weakened and a mutation proving the bound is still enforced; for (c): the limit is recorded under V1-0849 with the measured failure rates
body: Residual from the V1-1464/1000/1465 store-test lane (PR #965, head e26efb6fe, 2026-10-16). After the tests' own fixed waits became event-driven, TestPSRForegroundSignals still fails 10/34 subtests and TestPSRDispatchNativeAdapter 1/5 runs at load 56-88, all on fixed product bounds in internal/tasks: the sweep git observation 2 s bound (TIMEOUT; 4 ERROR runs and 3 OK runs with the member QUARANTINED "TIMEOUT; safe reuse failed"), the runner-identity 1 s bound (1 run), and the cleanup proof's WaitDelay/allowance giving "UNKNOWN; safe reuse failed" (2 runs). The V1-1324 load seam is package-private and the CLI is re-exec'd, so the cli tests cannot lift these bounds. Options: (a) scale the observation bound from --timeout-seconds; (b) add an exported or environment test seam (a production change); (c) accept as a ticketed load limit under V1-0849. Reproduction: `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestPSRForegroundSignals|TestPSRDispatchNativeAdapter' ./internal/tasks/cli` at load above 55.
title: Question: how should the pool-sweep product bounds (sweep git 2 s, runner identity 1 s, cleanup WaitDelay) behave under host load in the CLI signal/dispatch tests?
